paper_metadata.title: Experimental implementation of quantum-walk-based portfolio optimization

summary: The paper reports an experimental photonic implementation of the quantum-walk-based optimization algorithm (QWOA) for a 3-asset portfolio with 7 valid constrained solutions. Using 6 logical qubits encoded into a 7-dimensional qudit, the experiment shows the optimal-state probability increasing from 0.324 at p=1 to 0.797 ± 0.002 at p=6, with theory reaching 0.998, but it does not provide a classical baseline or demonstrate practical advantage.

experiments.description: Experimental implementation of the quantum-walk-based optimization algorithm (QWOA) for a 3-asset portfolio optimization problem using single-photon linear optics, evaluating probability amplification over circuit depths p=1 to 6.

algorithm.variant: Quantum-walk-based optimization algorithm (QWOA) with alternating phase-shift and continuous-time quantum walk unitaries
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial values for variational parameters γ and t generated uniformly at random in [0, 2π] for 20 repeats at each p

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: γ and t optimized with BFGS; initial values sampled uniformly in [0, 2π]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits per asset encode three positions: |10⟩ short, |01⟩ long, |00⟩ or |11⟩ no position; 6 qubits total for 3 assets, with a classically computed indexing of the 7 valid constrained solutions into a 7-dimensional qudit for the experiment
problem_formulation.objective_function: Mean-variance Markowitz cost C(s)=ω∑_{i,j=1}^M σ_{ij} z_i z_j − (1−ω)∑_{i=1}^M r_i z_i, with constraint ∑_{i=1}^M z_i = a
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraint a=0 enforced by restricting to the 7 valid solutions; valid solutions indexed classically and the walk acts only on the valid subspace

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over three stocks under a net-zero position constraint

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Adjusted closing prices used to compute expected returns and covariance matrix; quality values scaled by 250

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Expected returns and covariance matrix computed from daily closing/opening prices between 1/1/2019 and 12/31/2020; quality values q_i calculated classically from the mean-variance model and scaled by 250
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: For each p=1 to 6, compare theoretical and experimental output probability distributions and expectation value of the quality operator; photon counts recorded for 10 s per setting with approximately 27,000 single photons registered

noise_model.noise_type: interferometer imperfections and wave-plate inaccuracies; dephasing estimated at ~0.97

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of valid solution set, indexing, expected returns, covariance matrix, and optimal variational parameters via QuOp_MPI
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Projective measurement of photon counts to estimate basis-state probabilities and expectation value of the quality operator

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: objective value decreases with increasing p; probability of optimal state increases and stabilizes

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims reduced search space and practical applicability, but does not establish an asymptotic or empirical speedup over classical portfolio optimization methods.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A scalable photonic gate-based implementation of QWOA with low-loss interferometers, high-fidelity multi-mode unitaries, and a demonstrated classical-vs-quantum benchmark on larger portfolio instances than 3 assets would be needed.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline runtime or performance comparison is reported
Problem size is toy-scale: 3 assets, 7 valid solutions, 6 logical qubits
The paper reports only probability amplification and objective-value trends, not end-to-end advantage
Photonic implementation is experimental and sensitive to interferometer imperfections and wave-plate inaccuracies
Classical preprocessing is substantial: valid-solution indexing, expected returns, covariance matrix, and variational-parameter optimization are done classically

notes: Hardware identified as real_qpu_photonic because the paper reports an optical network with single photons, beam displacers, wave plates, and APD coincidence detection.

num_qubits reported as 7 because the experiment uses a 7-dimensional qudit encoding the 7 valid solutions; the underlying logical encoding is 6 qubits for 3 assets, but the implemented experimental register is 7 basis states.
Circuit depth is not explicitly given as a gate depth; p=1 to 6 iterations are reported, so num_layers is set to 6 and circuit_depth remains null.
Speedup order is none_proven because the paper discusses practical applicability and reduced search space but does not establish an asymptotic speedup over classical methods.

The paper demonstrates an experimental photonic realization of QWOA on a 3-asset portfolio and shows the optimal-state probability rising to about 0.998 in theory and 0.797 ± 0.002 experimentally at p=6.
No classical baseline is provided, so no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.
